judged_text: updateAllCalendarEvents resolves reference.credentialId via prisma.credential.findUnique with no ownership scoping, where the old code only matched credentials in this.calendarCredentials and got undefined (a handled no-op) for a foreign id. A booking reference carrying a credentialId foreign to the booking context now resolves to that credential and its OAuth key is used to update/move events in another user's calendar, activating stored reference data that was previously inert.

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents, when a calendar reference has reference.credentialId but no matching entry in this.calendarCredentials, the new code now falls back to prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: reference.credentialId } }) and then uses the returned credential (including its key) to call updateEvent(...). This lookup is by raw id only and shows no scoping/ownership check (e.g., booking.userId/teamId/org), so a booking/reference containing a foreign credentialId could cause the server to use another user's credential to update/delete calendar events. The finding matches the diff-grounded behavior change.
